title: NPDev model cross-reference index (npdev-model-xref.v1)
description: XREF-1. Every reference one model object makes to another, with an explicit three-state resolution. Produced by com.npdev.dsl.v1.xref.ReferenceIndexJson, which is the ONE writer: the generator emits it into each app as npdev/model-xref.json, and the :NPDevContract:dsl:modelXref Gradle task emits it for `npdev inspect usage`. Consumers: REG-185's ReferenceIntegrityValidation (errors on UNRESOLVED only), `npdev inspect usage` (XREF-2), and `npdev migrate rename --cascade` (XREF-3, which edits at each edge's `path`).

model.description: How this document names the model it describes -- the model file path for a CLI run, the namespace for a generated app. Free text; nothing parses it.

summary.description: Counts, so a consumer can report 'nothing unresolved' without walking every edge. `edges` always equals resolved + unresolved + undecidable.

edges.description: Sorted by `path`, then `toKind`, then `toName`. The order is part of the contract, not an accident: this file is emitted into every generated app and hashed across two generator runs by scripts/hygiene/check-deterministic-generation.ps1.

fromKind.description: Kind of the object making the reference.

fromName.description: Qualified name of the referencing object, exactly as the composed model spells it -- a pack-contributed panel reads `labeling::LabelPanel`.

site.description: The stable, dotted reference-BEARING key, independent of which instance carries it. Lets a consumer reason about a CLASS of reference; REG-185 uses it to skip sites other validators already cover, so one mistake never produces two errors.

path.description: Structural pointer to this exact occurrence. XREF-3's --cascade edits AT this pointer rather than string-replacing across the file, which is the difference between a rename and a corruption.

toName.description: For `field` targets, `Concept.field` (qualified concept included). For everything else the bare target name. For an UNDECIDABLE edge this is the RAW text that could not be evaluated, so a human can still read what was written.

ownerConcept.description: The concept a `field` target belongs to; null for other kinds. Carried separately so a consumer never has to re-split `toName` on a dot -- concept names may contain `::` but never `.`. Explicitly null rather than absent, because an absent key and a null key read the same to a careless consumer and only one of them is a promise.

resolution.description: RESOLVED: the target exists and `toName` names it. UNRESOLVED: well-formed reference, known target kind, no such target -- this is the orphan REG-185 errors on. UNDECIDABLE: could not be evaluated statically (an expression outside the interaction grammar, a `$var.field` whose producer declares no shape, an action input with no declaration surface). UNDECIDABLE is load-bearing and must never be rounded to either of the others: REG-185's origin was a validator in which 'we could not check this' and 'we checked and it was fine' printed identically.
